This is NPR News Now. The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News, I'm Giles Snyder. The Tennessee woman who survived a failed execution
is now awake. Reporter Katherine Sweeney at member station WPLN reports.
Krista Pike has been hospitalized since Wednesday. That's when Tennessee tried and failed to put her
to death for her role in the 1995 killing of Colleen Slimmer. The prison administered two doses
of lethal drugs, but she ultimately left in an ambulance. Her attorneys announced Tuesday
afternoon she was not only conscious but speaking. They said she was handcuffed to her bed even
though her arms are covered in burns and blisters. They attribute those injuries to bad IV placement
during her attempted execution and say it's likely the Pinto Barbatol intended to kill her
flowed into her flesh instead of into her bloodstream. For NPR News, I'm Katherine Sweeney in Nashville.
Pike's lawyers say they will be in court Wednesday. They are asking a judge for a court order to
preserve evidence from the failed execution, claiming the state of Tennessee violated
Pike's rights by subjecting her to cruel and unusual punishment. An execution date has been
set for the gunman who killed 13 people at Fort Hood, Texas in 2009 on social media. Acting Army
Secretary Adam Tell said that former Army psychiatrist Major Nidal Hassan will face a firing
squad on December 3rd. On Monday, a Pentagon spokesman said President Trump approved the use
of a firing squad at the recommendation of Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth. British police made another
arrest Tuesday, linked to a suspected plot to target an air base west of London. Police say
a 22-year-old British man remains in custody. Six others have been released on bail. On Monday,
President Trump acknowledged that a threat linked to Iran led the U.S. to remove its B-1 bombers
from the base and piers Tom Bowman is following the situation. So after these arrests, the U.S.
official said there was additional intelligence information about a credible threat by Iran
against the base, which hosted a dozen B-1 bombers, which of course had been taking part
in airstrikes on Iran. The threat was from drones, so the aircraft have returned to bases in the U.S.
And of course, already Iran has hit U.S. bases all around the Middle East with drones and missiles
damaging or destroying dozens of aircraft. You're looking at billions of dollars in damages.
President Trump has unveiled a major new investment in U.S. submarine production.
Here's NPR's Deepa Shivaraj. Trump gave remarks in Sparrow's Point,
an industrial site in Baltimore. While he was there to talk about a new $3.7 billion
private investment in growing U.S. submarine manufacturing, Trump also woven remarks about
Iran and Venezuela and his recent travel ahead of the midterms. The president's trip to Maryland
comes as his travel around the country has ramped up for the election, which is in less than a month.
He's expected to make trips to other states where Republicans are in close races,
including Alaska and Iowa. You're listening to NPR News.
To France now, riot police fired tear gas and used water cannons Tuesday as people packed the streets
for nationwide rallies over school funding. The government says more than a quarter million
marched in cities across the country to press for more education funding. The protests began
at a high school in the Paris region last month and have now grown into a nationwide movement.
A new study shows commercial kitchen appliances that use gas can expose workers to dangerous
levels of air pollution. From member station KQED, Azul Dholstrow-Meckman reports.
The first of its kind study compared air quality and temperature in kitchens that use gas appliances
to ones that are all electric. Out of 24 gas fired kitchens in Pennsylvania, New York and California,
70 percent had nitrogen dioxide levels above federal health guidelines. That can cause
respiratory illnesses. And four registered temperatures above 120 degrees. Yanai Kashtan
is with the nonprofit PSE Healthy Energy and is an author of the study. Commercial kitchens
with gas fired appliances have a lot higher levels of pollution and expose workers to more heat than
their electric counterparts. The study found the kitchens with all electric appliances had air
quality close to normal levels. For NPR News, I'm Azul Dholstrow-Meckman in San Francisco.
Asian stocks are losing ground in Wednesday trading. The retreat follows a record setting
day on Wall Street. The S&P 500 on Tuesday topped its all-time high set in August and

Krista Pike's lawyers seek court order to preserve evidence from failed execution
Former Army psychiatrist Nidal Hassan execution scheduled for December 3rd by firing squad
British police arrest 22-year-old man linked to suspected plot targeting London air base
U.S. removes B-1 bombers from British base following credible Iranian drone threat
President Trump announces $3.7 billion private investment in U.S. submarine manufacturing in Baltimore
French riot police deploy tear gas and water cannons during nationwide school funding protests
